about: 24-hour times read the way people say them (loop B139, CROSS X-051). BookLyre's 26 military-time cases from EpubToM4B tests/fixtures/spoken_military_times.json (auto/loop 9e49563, BACKLOG #209) in Backseat's own spoken numbers (no hyphens; years, counts and money as ForSpeech reads them), plus colon times: '22:00' is 'twenty two hundred', '13:00' 'thirteen hundred', '12:00'/'6:00' keep o'clock, '25:30' is not a time. Backseat Driver: backseat::pronunciation::ForSpeech / MilitaryTimes, NumberWords (libs/backseat/backseat_tests/pronunciation_test.cpp). BookLyre's negative cases (durations, years, rooms, out-of-range, money, '1430 h', 'hourses') are not military times here either; their expected values are Backseat's ordinary count/year/money reading of the digits.
